Account summary (Atlas Insurance)
- Enterprise carrier; internal AI platform team driving LLM standardization for claims + underwriting workflows.
- Current state: mixed vendor usage (pilot endpoints on cloud-managed, plus a self-hosted stack in one BU). Looking for predictable latency + cost + governance.

Workload / requirements
- Primary: long-form doc summarization + RAG on policy + claims docs (PDFs), plus "case notes" generation for adjusters.
- Latency: wants tight p95 for interactive flows; batch throughput also important for nightly backfills.
- Reliability: strong interest in automated fallback/compat models during capacity events (explicitly asked how Redwood handles regional failures and model pinning).
- Deployment: prefers VPC/private networking; will accept hosted for non-prod, but prod must be private/VPC with egress controls.
- Security: SSO/SAML, audit logs (who/what/when), retention controls, KMS integration, data residency (US). Procurement flagged data handling language.

Competitor notes / positioning
- They are comparing vs Bedrock (procurement likes the umbrella contract), Azure OpenAI (business users familiar), and 1–2 inference API vendors (Together/Fireworks mentioned in passing).
- Champion view: Redwood wins on "serving economics + operational control" (routing/fallback + observability). Procurement view: needs clear SLA + support terms to de-risk.

Reference / case study potential
- They are open to being a reference *if* (1) SLA/support addendum is signed and (2) they see 60–90 days of stable production.
- Likely reference format: private reference calls only at first; public case study could be anonymized or logo-only depending on comms/legal.
- Quote guidance (verbatim from 10/10 call): "We can talk about reliability and governance, but avoid hard $ numbers unless they’re ranges and we can approve the methodology." 

MAP (Mutual Action Plan) milestones (current)
1) Security + architecture review complete (VPC routing, audit logs, KMS) — IN PROGRESS
2) Dedicated sizing + SLO alignment (p95 latency, throughput) — IN PROGRESS
3) Commercial: MSA + DPA + Dedicated SLA/support addendum — IN PROGRESS (main blocker)
4) Pilot acceptance criteria + evaluation harness sign-off — PLANNED (target early Nov)
5) Exec sponsor review + procurement sign — PLANNED (target mid/late Nov)

Recent activity timeline
- 2025-09-12: Discovery w/ AI platform lead — confirmed use cases (claims summarization, RAG) and VPC requirement.
- 2025-09-24: Technical deep dive w/ SE (Markus) — discussed routing/fallback policies + observability needs.

- 2025-10-23: Commercial call — Atlas legal requested redlines on SLA credits + support response times; asked if we can commit to quarterly performance review.
